goal: Run a release-gate QA pass for the Tarot card library and the EN, offline/error, and backend-timeout paths on the connected Android phone before any release packaging decision.
successCriteria: The selected Tarot deck exposes all 78 unique cards on the device, and a card detail can open, navigate, and return without blank or duplicated content.
The EN locale renders Tarot library, reading, loading, fallback, and error copy without missing labels, clipping, or mixed-language blockers.
With network access disabled, a Tarot reading completes through the local fallback or shows a readable retry/error state without an indefinite spinner or duplicate credit/save action.
A controlled timeout test proves that the Tarot backend request aborts at its declared budget and returns the local fallback; the UI state is recorded on device where practical.
All findings have severity, sanitized device evidence, and a retest result; no production release, database migration, or remote write is performed.
untouchedSurfaces: Supabase migrations, credits schema, production endpoints, admin workspaces, authentication, payment entitlements, and public brand assets remain unchanged.
Canonical Tarot seed meanings, artwork prompts, and the 78-card content dataset remain unchanged unless QA proves a data defect that is separately approved.
No release upload, store submission, deployment, or irreversible remote action is included in this QA slice.

impact.entryPoint: Explore -> Tarot -> deck/library -> card detail, plus a new Tarot reading from topic, spread, deck, draw, and result; profile locale controls the EN pass.
impact.dataWrite: Device QA may create only synthetic local Tarot Journal entries needed to verify save/reopen behavior; no private user data is used.
impact.backendContract: The existing ai-tarot-reading request, abort signal, 75-second Tarot generation budget, and local fallback contract are tested; endpoint shape is not changed unless a verified UX fix requires it.
impact.canonicalContract: TarotStage, DrawnTarotCard, TarotInterpretationInput, generateTarotReading, and the 78-card seed dataset remain the canonical contracts.
impact.adminVisibility: No admin UI or operator contract changes; the report stores only sanitized route, locale, timing, and outcome fields.
impact.privacySafety: Questions and readings use fictional synthetic prompts; no raw account identifiers, private journal text, auth tokens, or backend payloads enter screenshots or logs.
impact.observability: Record build/version, device model, locale, route, elapsed time, network state, outcome, and severity in the QA report; preserve existing app telemetry.
impact.rollback: Revert any scoped App.tsx/backendClient.ts/test patch and remove only the QA report/plan if required; no migration or remote data rollback is needed.
impact.surfacesIntentionallyUntouched: Admin, backend schema, release publishing, deck content, and unrelated mobile routes are intentionally outside this pass.
impact.agentHandoff: The QA agent owns the scoped report and any minimal mobile timeout/fallback repair, runs static checks plus connected-device evidence, and stops at the release-readiness recommendation.

docs/CUSTOMER_PERSPECTIVE_QA.md defines sanitized customer scenarios, evidence, severity, and retest rules.

securityReview.authzRls: No authorization, RLS, migration, or protected endpoint behavior changes are planned.
securityReview.sensitiveData: Synthetic prompts only; device screenshots and logs are sanitized before being referenced in the report.
securityReview.secretsLogging: No credentials, auth headers, raw backend responses, or personal identifiers are recorded.
securityReview.externalInput: User-facing question and remote content remain untrusted display data; QA does not execute or persist arbitrary code.
securityReview.dependencies: No dependency installation is required for the QA pass.
securityReview.migrationRelease: No database repair, database push, release upload, deployment, or publishing action is planned.
securityReview.stopCondition: Stop if a private payload appears in evidence, the local fallback violates safety copy, a migration/release action becomes necessary, or a high-risk blocker cannot be isolated.

managerTestPath: On the connected Android phone, open Explore -> Tarot -> the deck library, confirm 78 distinct card names and open a card detail; switch to EN and repeat the visible labels; disable network, start a one-card synthetic reading, confirm a readable fallback/error and no endless spinner; review the timeout test timing and release recommendation in docs/TAROT_RELEASE_QA_2026-09-29.vi.md.
residualRisk: A local internal QA APK is not a release artifact; native build signing, store packaging, backend production latency, and remote entitlement behavior remain separate release gates.
